newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai interbank rate eases, baht down late.
newsitem.headline: Thai interbank rate eases, baht down late.

text.p: The Thai overnight interbank rate eased to 6.00 percent late on Monday from 6.75-7.00 earlier and 6.25-6.50 percent late on Friday amid high liquidity, dealers said.
"The interbank rate was higher to 7.00 percent in the morning. Then it declined as most banks tried to dispose of their excess funds in the afternoon," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
Dealers said the high liquidity was attributed to government budget disbursements for the new fiscal period which began October 1, and to money from recent sales on the stock market.
The baht fell to 25.464-25.467 to the dollar near the close from 25.457-25.460 early as high baht supply and low baht short-term interest rates prompted demand for the U.S. unit, dealers said.
News of Finance Minister Bodi Chunnananda's resignation had no impact on the market, said another U.S. bank dealer.
"The short-term baht interest rates is very low. This made people shift to hold the dollar," said one currency dealer. "But the dollar buying is moderate today."

Finance Minister Bodi Chunnananda on Monday submitted his resignation to Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa. He did not state the reasons for his unexpected resignation that will take effect on Tuesday.
Banharn's spokesman said the premier had not yet seen the resignation letter but if it was true than the deputy minister Chaiyawat Wibulswasdi would be the care-taker minister.

Dealers see no impact on the baht from the finance minister's resignation because there will no major policy from any caretaker minister who would eventually be replaced after the general election next month.
"I don't think there will be any impact (on the baht). He is a caretaker and is unlikely to implement any significant policy if he stays on until the election," said one senior dealer at a U.S. bank.
The one-month baht/dollar swap premium was quoted at 7.50/8.50 satangs per dollar late from 7.25/8.00 in early morning.
The mid-rate was fixed at 25.45 to the dollar against 25.44 on Friday.
